title: Les Faux Amis
description: False friends between French and English.

items.translation: Words that look like English words but mean something else
items.exampleFr: « Actuellement » ne veut pas dire « actually ».

items.exampleEn: He is currently working in Lyon.

items.prompt: What does “attendre” really mean?
items.explain: “to attend” is “assister à”. J'attends le bus. — I am waiting for the bus.

items.prompt: “assister à” does not mean “to assist”. Type the real French for “to assist”.
items.explain: “assister à” means “to attend”. J'ai assisté à la réunion. — I attended the meeting.

items.exampleFr: J'achète mes livres à la librairie.
items.exampleEn: I buy my books at the bookshop.

items.prompt: What does “la monnaie” really mean?
items.explain: “money” is “l'argent”. Vous avez de la monnaie ? — Do you have any change?

items.prompt: “rester” does not mean “to rest”. Type the real French for “to rest”.
items.explain: “rester” means “to stay”. Je reste à la maison ce soir. — I am staying at home tonight.

items.exampleEn: He is a very sensitive child.

items.prompt: What does “éventuellement” really mean?
items.explain: “eventually” is “finalement”. Je pourrais éventuellement venir. — I could possibly come.

items.prompt: “la journée” does not mean “the journey”. Type the real French for “the journey”.
items.explain: “la journée” means “the day”. J'ai passé une bonne journée. — I had a good day.

items.exampleFr: La boulangerie est au coin de la rue.
items.exampleEn: The bakery is on the corner of the street.

items.prompt: What does “blesser” really mean?
items.explain: “to bless” is “bénir”. Il s'est blessé au genou. — He injured his knee.

items.prompt: “passer un examen” does not mean “to pass an exam”. Type the real French for “to pass an exam”.
items.explain: “passer un examen” means “to sit an exam”. Je passe un examen demain. — I am sitting an exam tomorrow.

items.exampleFr: La location de voiture coûte cher.

items.prompt: What does “demander” really mean?
items.explain: “to demand” is “exiger”. Je vais demander le prix. — I am going to ask the price.

items.prompt: “la lecture” does not mean “the lecture”. Type the real French for “the lecture”.
items.explain: “la lecture” means “reading”. La lecture est mon passe-temps. — Reading is my hobby.

items.prompt: What does “la cave” really mean?
items.explain: “the cave” is “la grotte”. Le vin est à la cave. — The wine is in the cellar.

items.prompt: “le car” does not mean “the car”. Type the real French for “the car”.
items.explain: “le car” means “the coach (bus)”. Nous prenons le car pour Nice. — We are taking the coach to Nice.

items.exampleEn: He claims to be a doctor.

items.prompt: What does “la déception” really mean?
items.explain: “deception” is “la tromperie”. Quelle déception ! — What a disappointment!

items.prompt: “formidable” does not mean “formidable”. Type the real French for “formidable”.
items.explain: “formidable” means “great / wonderful”. C'est une idée formidable ! — That is a great idea!

items.prompt: What does “le médecin” really mean?
items.explain: “the medicine” is “le médicament”. Je vais chez le médecin. — I am going to the doctor's.

items.prompt: “la chair” does not mean “the chair”. Type the real French for “the chair”.
items.explain: “la chair” means “flesh”. La chair de ce poisson est tendre. — The flesh of this fish is tender.

items.prompt: J'achète un roman à la ___.
J'emprunte un roman à la ___.
Je n'ai pas de ___ pour le parking.
Elle a ___ son examen : elle a eu 18 sur 20 !
Il travaille ___ sur un nouveau projet.
J'___ mon ami devant le cinéma.
